reason: Rewrite the product as N(q)/D(q) with N = product_{i=a+1}^b (q^(r+i)-1) and D = product_{i=a+1}^b (q^i-1). For a primitive d-th root of unity zeta, the multiplicity of zeta in q^m-1 is 1 exactly when d divides m, and otherwise 0. Hence the multiplicities of zeta in N and D are exactly the two floor differences in the statement. If the quotient is a polynomial, multiplicities in N dominate those in D, giving the floor inequalities. Conversely, if the inequalities hold for every d, then every root of D appears in N with at least the same multiplicity, so D divides N in C[q]; since D is monic and N,D have integer coefficients, long division gives the quotient in Z[q].
